## Reference solution

The reference solution is the **Crossplane restaurant** — the canonical worked
example for this course. It is not a copy-paste answer; it shows what a
complete, passing project looks like across every phase and artifact. Read it
alongside your own project and compare.

| Phase (Lab Method) | Reference artifact |
| --- | --- |
| Observe / Investigate | `reference-example/concept.md` |
| Design | `reference-example/metaphor.md` |
| Compose | `reference-example/characters.md`, `scenes.md`, `screenplay.md` |
| Execute | `reference-example/production.md`, `output/` |
| Evaluate | `reference-example/evaluation.md` |
| Reflect | your own `reflection.md` |

### How the reference satisfies the objectives

- **Technical truth first.** `concept.md` describes the Crossplane model (XRD,
  claim, XR, Composition, Managed Resources, Provider, reconciliation) with no
  restaurant imagery — a clean model precedes any metaphor.
- **Isomorphic metaphor.** `metaphor.md` maps XRD→Menu, XR→Order,
  Composition→Recipe, Managed Resources→Prepared components, Provider→Kitchen
  capability, with a rationale per row and no serious misconception.
- **Small, distinct cast.** Five voices, one per responsibility, each with
  voice and relationship; the developer never talks to providers.
- **Scene-oriented with learning outcomes.** Seven scenes, each with a purpose
  and an answer to "what did the learner understand?".
- **Audio-first screenplay.** Every action reaches the ear; semantic sound
  design maps sounds to model events (ticket printer → claim created, recipe
  book → composition selected, service bell → successful reconciliation,
  kitchen alarm → failure).
- **Provider-neutral production.** `production.md` declares neutral
  capabilities and documents Wondercraft only as the validated implementation.
- **Evaluation with weighted technical accuracy.** The five-dimension rubric is
  applied, with technical accuracy weighted highest, and defects traced to
  their origin stage.

## Verification

You can verify the reference yourself by reverse-engineering it, as Module 1
teaches:

1. Read the final `screenplay.md` (or listen to the produced audio).
2. For each scene, identify the technical concept it teaches.
3. Check that every element (character, sound, narration) maps back through
   `metaphor.md` to an entity in `concept.md` without contradiction.
4. Score the result with the five-dimension rubric and confirm no serious
   technical inaccuracy.

A passing project of yours will show the same properties — on your own concept.

## A note on your own artifact

Your `output/audio-play.mp3` is a **2–5 minute educational audio drama**. Raw
binary audio need not be committed to Git if size or licensing makes that
undesirable; follow the Open Engineering artifact conventions in that case and
link to the artifact instead. The **text artifacts** (concept, metaphor,
characters, scenes, screenplay, production, evaluation, reflection) are the
primary reviewable deliverable.

## Variations

- **Different world:** any isomorphic metaphor (theatre, airport, orchestra)
  is valid as long as the mapping stays honest.
- **Different renderer:** another AI audio service, human actors, or studio
  production is fine — the screenplay is renderer-independent.
- **Deferred Composer:** a future Composer could generate a first screenplay
  draft from the model; your artifacts are structured so this remains possible,
  but human review of metaphor and narrative stays essential.
